chapters.title: THE METHODS OF TESTING PRECIOUS STONES
chapters.exactFinalPrompt:
Use case: historical-scene
Asset type: final independent replacement Naturalis Historia Book XXXVII chapter 13 illustration master
Primary request: Create a visibly hand-drawn Roman-era Plinian folio scene of detecting a counterfeit precious stone, grounded in morning-light, weight, internal-bubble, surface, and hardness tests. Do not show the mouth-cooling test or provide modern testing advice.
Scene/backdrop: one austere open-front lapidary room at early morning. A broad diagonal band of cool dawn light crosses an otherwise empty continuous ochre plaster wall and plain stone floor. The background contains no shelf, side table, cabinet, pottery, container, window frame, arch, inset, water, or extra object.
Subject: exactly two complete mature adults total: one seated gem examiner and one standing merchant, both fully visible from head through sandals. Their tunics and mantles are plain solid mineral colors with absolutely no border pattern, embroidered marks, symbols, repeated motifs, lettering, or decorative trim. The examiner holds one complete translucent imitation jewel in the light between finger and thumb; it shows one small internal bubble and subtly uneven brilliance. Centered between the adults is one complete low wooden table, fully visible including every leg. On it stands one complete ancient two-pan balance, fully visible: one pan holds one pale genuine crystal and hangs slightly lower, the other holds one same-sized glass imitation and hangs slightly higher. Beside it lie one complete dark obsidian touchstone and one complete blunt iron graver, both unused. No other stone, tool, furniture, or prop appears.
Style/medium: unmistakably a hand-illuminated natural-history folio, never a lifelike oil painting—warm fibrous aged vellum visibly showing through; firm iron-gall ink outlines around every form; dense directional cross-hatching on faces, cloth, wood, and plaster; stippled mineral surfaces; dry-brush abrasion; flattened manuscript depth; thin translucent washes; restrained matte highlights only. Palette: umber, lampblack, muted verdigris, faded lapis, madder, ochre, rock-crystal ivory, tiny jewel accents. Ancient, timeless, beautiful, rough in material and polished in draftsmanship.
Composition/framing: spacious three-quarter view with the diagonal dawn beam and a triangular examiner-balance-merchant rhythm. Ample negative space. One coherent continuous scene. Every person, hand, foot, chair, table leg, balance, pan, stone, touchstone, and graver is complete and separated from every canvas edge by generous margins. Native landscape 3:2, 1536x1024, opaque RGB/sRGB.
Lighting/mood: lucid early-morning scrutiny, skeptical and calm.
Text: none.
Constraints: exactly two living people, one chair, one table, one balance, two balance-pan stones, one raised imitation jewel, one touchstone, one graver; historically plausible Roman material culture. Ancient craft testimony only.
Avoid: smooth realistic skin, cinematic oil painting, photography, photorealism, glossy CGI, decorative clothing, patterned hems, pseudo-writing, lettering, numerals, labels, inscriptions, scale markings, signatures, watermarks, border, dark perimeter line, depicted page, inset, panels, collage, diagram, side furniture, side props, pottery, magnifying glass, microscope, modern jewelry tools, clipped subject, duplicated hands, duplicated gems, mouth contact, injury, flame, or magical glow.
